reason: Phagocytes are shown engulfing debris near the cut, so they seem a useful first step in clearing the wound.
expectation: The phagocytes will begin clearing debris from the wound.

effect: The wound is cleared of debris and now needs supply, surface and support fitted.
reaction: The named slots make the next stages clear.
reason: Repair signals point to the nearby vessel, suggesting they help establish the wound's blood supply.
expectation: The signals will prompt the capillary to grow toward the wound.

effect: The repair signals produced a capillary sprout connected to the existing circulation, which looks suitable for the supply slot.
reaction: The connection to the parent vessel makes the new supply easier to picture.
reason: The capillary sprout appears to provide the wound's blood supply.
expectation: The sprout will fit the supply slot and bring blood toward the wound.

effect: The capillary sprout now forms a connected flow route that can supply the developing tissue.
reaction: The completed loop makes the supply role clear.
reason: Fibroblasts need raw materials to build the wound's supporting matrix.
expectation: The fibroblasts will use the nutrients to build supporting tissue.

effect: Fibroblasts used the materials to make new connective tissue, which appears to fill the support slot.
reaction: The collagen fibres make the support role clear.
reason: The new connective tissue should support the damaged dermis.
expectation: The connective tissue will fit the support slot in the wound.

effect: The connective tissue fills the support role, though the new tissue is not yet as strong as uninjured skin.
reaction: The distinction between closing the wound and restoring strength is useful.
reason: The epidermal edge cells appear to need nutrients to rebuild the wound surface.
expectation: The cells will use the nutrients to form a new surface layer.

effect: The edge cells formed a new epidermal sheet that appears ready for the surface slot.
reaction: The sheet extending across the gap makes the closure easy to picture.
reason: The new surface should close the remaining gap in the healing skin.
expectation: The new surface will fill the surface slot and close the wound.

effect: The new surface spans the gap, completing the wound's closure, support and supply; the temporary clot still needs clearing.
reaction: It is useful that the result distinguishes a closed surface from deeper tissue still gaining strength.
reason: Clot-clearing enzymes are shown breaking down fibrin, so they should clear the temporary clot.
expectation: The enzymes will break down the fibrin in the clot.

effect: The enzymes cleared most of the temporary fibrin, completing the chapter while leaving a scar that is still maturing.
reaction: The remaining scar makes the repair feel like a continuing process rather than an instant return to uninjured skin.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the capillary sprout was most worthwhile: the described flow loop and nutrient arrows made the wound's need for a blood supply concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making and fitting the new surface felt predictable after the named slots and earlier support construction, although the picture description made closure clear.

surprise.text: The distinction between a closed surface and deeper tissue still gaining strength changed my understanding of what completing the wound means.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the item descriptions and named slots gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it explored a new relationship with a concrete sequence like the wound's supply and repair. The repeated build-and-slot pattern could become less engaging if it continued unchanged.
